source.title: Local politics banks written for Prospero's Companion
source.note: Ported from Prospero's Companion (#457) with Dungeon's own `world_kinds`.

modern.title: Housing costs
modern.question: Should the city build homes on its own land, even in the nicer neighborhoods?
beats: Rents rose again this month.
A new block was turned down after neighbors objected.
A family in {hood} was priced out after twenty years.
Builders say the rules are too tight.
A packed council meeting ran past midnight.

modern.title: Bike lanes
modern.question: Should parking spaces make way for bike lanes?
beats: A cyclist was hit in {hood}.
Shop owners say lanes are killing trade.
A new lane opened downtown.

modern.title: The police budget
modern.question: Should the city spend more on police or on everything else?

sides.name: Spend it elsewhere
sides.stand: spend it on schools and clinics

beats: Break-ins are up in {hood}.
An arrest was filmed and shared everywhere.
The budget vote is coming.

modern.title: Holiday rentals
modern.question: Should holiday rentals be limited?
beats: Half a street in {hood} is holiday rentals now.
Owners say the money keeps them afloat.

modern.title: Machines taking jobs
modern.question: Should companies pay a tax for every job a machine takes?

sides.name: No tax
sides.stand: let companies get on with it

beats: A warehouse let half its staff go.
A new firm opened with almost nobody working there.
Prices fell at the shops.

modern.title: The heat
modern.question: Should the city ban cars from the center on hot days?
beats: Another record hot day.
Deliveries were stuck outside the center.

jazz.title: Prohibition
jazz.question: Should the country stay dry?
beats: Prohibition agents raided a club in {hood}.
A batch of bad liquor sent people to the hospital.
A judge was seen drinking at {place}.
Gangs fought over the trade in {hood}.
A padlocked club reopened next door under a new name.
A preacher led a march against the speakeasies.

jazz.title: Closing the door
jazz.question: Should the country keep letting immigrants in?
beats: A ship was turned back at the harbor.
Families in {hood} wait on news of relatives.

jazz.title: The machine at City Hall
jazz.question: Should the party machine keep running the city?

sides.name: The machine delivers
sides.stand: keep the machine; it looks after people

beats: A ward boss handed out coal in {hood}.
A reform candidate was beaten up.
The paper printed who got the city jobs.

jazz.title: The unions
jazz.question: Should workers be free to join a union?
beats: A strike closed a works in {hood}.
Strikebreakers were brought in by train.

jazz.title: The new woman
jazz.question: Should young women live as freely as young men?

sides.name: Let them
sides.stand: let young women live as they like

beats: A dance marathon in {hood} scandalized the papers.
A preacher railed against bobbed hair.

victorian.title: Votes for women
victorian.question: Should women have the vote?

sides.name: Antis
sides.stand: keep the vote as it is

beats: A suffrage meeting filled the hall at {place}.
A petition was laughed out of the chamber.
A woman chained herself to the railings.

victorian.title: Temperance
victorian.question: Should the drink trade be curbed?
beats: A temperance band played outside {place}.
A gin shop in {hood} was fined.
Brewers paid for a free supper.

victorian.title: The hours bill
victorian.question: Should the working day be limited by law?

sides.name: Free trade
sides.stand: leave it to masters and men

beats: A mill hand collapsed at the end of a shift.
Masters say it will ruin them.

victorian.title: Home rule
victorian.question: Should the far province govern itself?
beats: A speech on home rule drew a crowd and a riot.
The bill was thrown out again.

victorian.title: The great stink
victorian.question: Should rates rise to pay for drains and clean water?
beats: Cholera in {hood}.
Ratepayers met to protest the cost.

frontier.title: The railroad
frontier.question: Should the town give land to bring the railroad through?

sides.name: Bring it
sides.stand: give the land and bring the railroad

beats: Surveyors were seen west of town.
A rancher refused to sell.
A rival town offered more land.

frontier.title: Statehood
frontier.question: Should the territory seek statehood?
beats: A convention was called.
Ranchers say taxes would ruin them.

frontier.title: Fencing the range
frontier.question: Should the open range be fenced?
beats: Fences were cut overnight.
A herd died at a fenced water hole.
A homesteader was threatened.

frontier.title: Closing the saloons
frontier.question: Should the saloons be closed?
beats: A woman with a hatchet smashed up a saloon.
A shooting at {place}.
Saloon keepers raised money for the town.

frontier.title: The land office
frontier.question: Is the land office favoring the big outfits?

sides.name: It is
sides.stand: see the land office cleaned up

beats: A claim was jumped.
The land agent dined with the big rancher.

medieval.title: The crown's new tax
medieval.question: Should the town pay the crown's new war tax?
beats: The tax collectors came through {hood}.
A collector was beaten and sent off.
Soldiers were seen on the road.

medieval.title: The town charter
medieval.question: Should the town buy a charter to govern itself?
beats: The guilds met in secret.
The lord's steward warned against it.

medieval.title: The abbey's land
medieval.question: Should the abbey keep its fields tax-free?
beats: The abbey fenced off a common field.
The abbot fed the poor at the gate.

medieval.title: The war abroad
medieval.question: Should the town send men to the king's war?
beats: A herald read the king's summons in {hood}.
Word came of a lost battle.

fantasy.title: The old peoples
fantasy.question: Should the old peoples be welcome in town as equals?
beats: A fight at {place} between townsfolk and travelers.
An elder of the old peoples spoke in the square.

fantasy.title: Taxing magic
fantasy.question: Should magic-workers pay a tax to the crown?
beats: A tax collector visited a hedge-witch in {hood}.
A healer refused to pay and kept working.

fantasy.title: Rumors of war
fantasy.question: Should the town arm itself against the empire across the water?

sides.name: Trade, not war
sides.stand: keep trading and keep the peace

beats: Sails were seen off the coast.
A trade treaty was signed.
Spies were taken in {hood}.

fantasy.title: The temple's power
fantasy.question: Should the temple have a say in the town's laws?

sides.name: No say
sides.stand: keep the temple out of the law

beats: The high priest spoke against a new law.
A temple court sentenced a merchant.
A merchant refused to pay the temple.

future.title: The ration
future.question: Should the ration be cut to build up the reserves?

sides.name: Cut it
sides.stand: cut the ration and build reserves

beats: A crop failed in the farm rings.
The reserve figures were posted.

future.title: Where we're going
future.question: Should the course be changed for the closer world?
beats: New readings came in about the closer world.
The founders' charter was read aloud.

future.title: Birth permits
future.question: Should birth permits be eased?
beats: A couple was refused a permit.
Air figures came in lower than hoped.

future.title: Who runs the ship
future.question: Should the crew council have the final word over command?

sides.name: Crew council
sides.stand: give the council the final word

beats: Command overruled the council.
A fault was fixed fast on command's order.

local.title: The {office} and the {institution} money
local.question: Did the {office} skim money meant for the {institution}?

sides.name: Stands by them
sides.stand: leave the {office} be until there is proof

beats.whispers: People whisper that money for the {institution} never reached it.
beats.open: Ledgers from the {institution} show sums gone missing on the {office}'s watch.
beats.heated: A crowd gathers outside the {institution}; the {office} is called to answer.
beats.won: The {office} steps down and the {institution} gets its money back.
beats.lost: The {office} is cleared, and the talk turns sour on the accusers.
beats.fizzled: Nobody can prove anything, and the {institution} limps on.

local.title: Who got the paving contract
local.question: Did the {office2} hand the road contract to a friend?

sides.name: Wants it rebid
sides.stand: see the contract opened up again

sides.name: Let it stand
sides.stand: let the work go ahead as awarded

beats.whispers: The firm paving {hood} belongs to the {office2}'s brother-in-law, people say.
beats.open: The paper prints who owns the paving firm.
beats.heated: Half-finished roads in {hood} make it everyone's business.
beats.won: The contract is torn up and put out to bid again.
beats.lost: The contract stands and the roads get finished.
beats.fizzled: The roads get finished and nobody asks any more.

local.title: Paying off the {office2}
local.question: Are shopkeepers in {hood} paying the {office2} to look the other way?

sides.name: Clean it up
sides.stand: clean out whoever is taking money

sides.name: Leave it be
sides.stand: keep things as they are; it keeps the peace

beats.whispers: A shopkeeper in {hood} lets slip what they pay each month.
beats.open: Someone names names in the paper.
beats.heated: A shop that refused to pay is smashed up overnight.
beats.won: The {office2} is replaced and the payments stop.
beats.lost: Nothing changes; the shopkeepers keep paying.
beats.fizzled: The talk dies down and so do the names.

local.title: The new levy
local.question: Should the {office} raise a new levy to pay for the {institution}?

sides.name: For the levy
sides.stand: pay a bit more and keep the {institution} going

sides.name: Against it
sides.stand: keep the money in people's pockets

beats.whispers: Word is the {office} wants a new levy.
beats.open: The levy is put up for a vote.
beats.heated: Shopkeepers threaten to close in protest.
beats.won: The levy passes and the {institution} is saved.
beats.lost: The levy fails; the {institution} cuts back.
beats.fizzled: The vote is put off and the levy forgotten.

local.title: The missing ledger
local.question: Who took the {office2}'s account book, and what was in it?

sides.name: Wants it found
sides.stand: see the books opened to everyone

sides.name: Drop it
sides.stand: let it lie; nothing good comes of digging

beats.whispers: An account book went missing from the {office2}'s office.
beats.open: {person} says they have seen pages from it.
beats.heated: Torn pages turn up nailed to doors in {hood}.
beats.won: The book is found and the {office2} has some explaining to do.
beats.lost: The book stays lost and {person} is called a liar.
beats.fizzled: Nobody finds it and nobody asks.

local.title: Cutting the old-age fund
local.question: Should the {office} cut the fund that keeps old workers fed?

sides.name: Keep the fund
sides.stand: leave the old workers' fund alone

sides.name: Cut it
sides.stand: cut it back before it sinks the budget

beats.whispers: There is talk of cuts to the old workers' fund.
beats.open: The {office} names the cuts.
beats.heated: Old workers march on the {office}'s door.
beats.fizzled: The cuts are put off for another year.

local.title: Short weights at the market
local.question: Are the {trade} cheating buyers with short weights?

sides.name: Trust the trade
sides.stand: let the {trade} keep their own scales

beats.whispers: A loaf weighed at home comes up short.
beats.open: The {office2} is asked to test the market scales.
beats.heated: A fight breaks out at a stall in {hood}.
beats.won: Every scale is checked and two stalls are shut.
beats.lost: The {trade} are cleared and the complaint looks petty.
beats.fizzled: People just weigh things at home now.

local.title: A bought vote
local.question: Did the {office} win by buying votes in {hood}?

sides.name: The vote stands
sides.stand: accept the result and move on

beats.whispers: People in {hood} say they were paid to vote.
beats.open: The paper prints how many votes {hood} cast, more than it has people.
beats.heated: A recount is demanded at the courthouse.
beats.won: A recount is ordered and the result is overturned.
beats.lost: The result stands and the matter is closed.
beats.fizzled: Nobody pays for a recount and it all blows over.

local.title: The back room at {place}
local.question: Should the back-room gambling at {place} be shut down?

sides.name: Shut it down
sides.stand: close the back room for good

sides.name: Let them play
sides.stand: let people spend their own money

beats.whispers: Everyone knows there is a game in the back of {place}.
beats.open: A man loses his house at the tables, and the paper says where.
beats.heated: The {office2} is seen at the tables.
beats.lost: The game goes on, more open than ever.
beats.fizzled: The game moves somewhere else and the fuss with it.

local.title: Where the ball money went
local.question: Did the charity ball's money really go to the {institution}?

sides.name: Leave the committee alone
sides.stand: trust the committee; they are good people

beats.whispers: The ball raised a fortune, but the {institution} saw little of it.
beats.open: The committee will not show its books.
beats.heated: Two committee members fall out in public.
beats.won: The books are opened and the money is paid over.
beats.fizzled: Next year's ball is quietly cancelled.

local.title: The new dock fees
local.question: Should the {office} double the fees at the docks?

sides.name: Raise them
sides.stand: make the shippers pay their share

sides.name: Leave them
sides.stand: keep the fees where they are

beats.whispers: The {office} wants more from the docks.
beats.open: The new fees are posted.
beats.heated: Ships start unloading somewhere cheaper.
beats.won: The fees go up and the city's coffers fill.
beats.lost: The fees are dropped after a week of empty quays.
beats.fizzled: The fees are halved and everyone grumbles.

local.title: The fire brigade fund
local.question: Where did the money for the new fire engine go?

sides.name: Wants it back
sides.stand: see the money found and the engine bought

beats.whispers: The fire brigade is still waiting for its engine.
beats.open: The money was spent, the paper says, but not on an engine.
beats.heated: A fire in {hood} burns longer than it should have.
beats.won: The engine is bought at last.
beats.lost: The brigade is told to make do.
beats.fizzled: The engine arrives a year late and nobody remembers why.

local.title: Fines that went missing
local.question: Has the {office2} been pocketing the fines?

sides.name: Nonsense
sides.stand: leave the {office2} to do the job

beats.whispers: Fines are paid, but the city's books do not show them.
beats.open: {person} shows a receipt that was never entered.
beats.heated: The {office2} threatens to sue.
beats.won: The {office2} is let go and the money paid back.
beats.fizzled: Nobody checks and the fines keep coming.

local.title: Who sells the salt
local.question: Should one house keep the right to sell all the salt?

sides.name: Keep the charter
sides.stand: keep the old charter as it is

beats.whispers: Salt is dearer than last year and everyone knows why.
beats.open: A peddler is fined for selling salt in {hood}.
beats.heated: Salt carts are overturned at the gate.
beats.won: The charter is broken and salt gets cheaper.
beats.fizzled: Salt stays dear and people stop complaining.

local.title: Skimming the ration stores
local.question: Is someone in supply taking more than their share?

sides.name: Trust supply
sides.stand: let supply run its own stores

beats.whispers: The stores are coming up short, people say.
beats.open: The {office2} admits the counts do not add up.
beats.heated: Crew in {hood} refuse their shift until there is an answer.
beats.won: An audit finds the leak and plugs it.
beats.lost: Supply is cleared and the counts are blamed on a fault.
beats.fizzled: The counts come right on their own and the talk stops.

local.title: The new line through {hood}
local.question: Should the new line run straight through {hood}?

sides.name: Build it
sides.stand: build the line and bring the city closer

beats.whispers: Surveyors are seen measuring streets in {hood}.
beats.open: The plans are posted: the line runs right through {hood}.
beats.heated: Residents of {hood} block the surveyors.
beats.won: The line is approved and work begins.
beats.fizzled: The plans are shelved for now.

local.title: Tearing down {place}
local.question: Should {place} come down to make room for something new?

sides.name: Tear it down
sides.stand: clear it and build something better

beats.whispers: A buyer is said to want {place}.
beats.open: The sale of {place} is announced.
beats.heated: People chain themselves to the doors of {place}.
beats.fizzled: The buyer loses interest.

local.title: The tower over {hood}
local.question: Should a tall tower go up in {hood}?

sides.name: Build it
sides.stand: build up and make room for more people

beats.whispers: A developer has bought a corner in {hood}.
beats.open: The plans show a tower three times the height of anything near it.
beats.heated: A packed meeting in {hood} turns to shouting.
beats.fizzled: The developer goes quiet and the corner stays empty.

local.title: Selling the green in {hood}
local.question: Should the city sell the green in {hood} to builders?

sides.name: Sell it
sides.stand: sell it and spend the money on the city

beats.whispers: A builder has been seen walking the green in {hood}.
beats.open: The {office} puts the green up for sale.
beats.heated: Children's games are staged on the green every evening in protest.
beats.fizzled: Nobody bids and the green stays.

local.title: Capping rents
local.question: Should the city cap how much rents can rise?

sides.name: No cap
sides.stand: let landlords set their own rents

beats.whispers: Rents in {hood} jumped again this month.
beats.open: A cap is proposed at City Hall.
beats.heated: Tenants in {hood} stop paying rent together.
beats.fizzled: The cap is sent to a committee and never comes back.

local.title: The mill on the river
local.question: Should the new mill be allowed to dam the river?

sides.name: Build the mill
sides.stand: let the mill go up and bring the work

beats.whispers: There is talk of a new mill upriver.
beats.open: The mill's owners ask for the right to dam the river.
beats.heated: Fishermen and farmers block the road to the site.
beats.fizzled: The mill's money dries up and the plan with it.

local.title: Mending the walls
local.question: Should everyone be made to give a week's work to mend the walls?

sides.name: Mend them
sides.stand: mend the walls before trouble comes

sides.name: Pay for it
sides.stand: hire masons instead of taking people's work

beats.whispers: Stones are falling from the wall by {hood}.
beats.open: The {office} calls for a week's work from every household.
beats.heated: Whole streets fail to turn up.
beats.won: The walls are mended by the town's own hands.
beats.fizzled: The work is put off until spring.

local.title: A new bridge
local.question: Should the city build a new bridge to {hood}?

sides.name: Not worth it
sides.stand: spend the money on what we already have

beats.whispers: There is talk of a bridge to {hood}.
beats.open: Plans for the bridge are shown at {place}.
beats.heated: The cost doubles, and so does the arguing.
beats.fizzled: The plans gather dust.

local.title: Clearing the old blocks in {hood}
local.question: Should the oldest blocks in {hood} be cleared?

sides.name: Clear them
sides.stand: clear them and build decent homes

beats.whispers: Inspectors are seen in the old blocks of {hood}.
beats.open: The blocks are declared unfit.
beats.heated: Families refuse to leave.
beats.fizzled: The work is put off another year.

local.title: Opening the new ring
local.question: Should the empty ring be opened for families, or kept for cargo?

sides.name: Keep it for cargo
sides.stand: keep it for cargo and spare parts

beats.whispers: The sealed ring has been checked over, people say.
beats.open: The {office} asks for views on the ring.
beats.heated: Families camp at the ring's hatch.
beats.won: The ring is opened for homes.
beats.lost: The ring is kept for cargo.
beats.fizzled: The question is put off until the next refit.

local.title: Moving the market
local.question: Should the market move out of {hood}?

sides.name: Keep it here
sides.stand: keep the market where it has always been

beats.whispers: The {office} thinks the market has outgrown {hood}.
beats.open: A new site is named.
beats.heated: Stallholders refuse to pack up.
beats.fizzled: Nobody moves and nobody makes them.

local.title: The great sewer
local.question: Should the city borrow to build a proper sewer?

sides.name: Build it
sides.stand: build it and be done with the stink

sides.name: Too costly
sides.stand: not borrow the city into ruin

beats.whispers: The smell in {hood} is worse than any summer before.
beats.open: An engineer's plan is put before the city.
beats.heated: Fever in {hood} turns the argument.
beats.won: The loan is raised and digging begins.
beats.fizzled: A smaller plan is made instead.

local.title: Who pays for the light
local.question: Should the merchants or the city pay to keep the harbor light?

sides.name: Merchants pay
sides.stand: make the merchants pay for their own light

sides.name: City pays
sides.stand: have the city pay for the light

beats.whispers: The harbor light went dark two nights running.
beats.open: The keeper says nobody has paid him.
beats.heated: A boat runs aground in the dark.
beats.fizzled: The keeper pays for oil himself, for now.

local.title: Closing time
local.question: Should the taverns close earlier?

beats.whispers: There have been fights outside {place} every week.
beats.open: Earlier closing is proposed.
beats.heated: The tavern keepers organize.
beats.won: Closing time comes an hour earlier.
beats.lost: The hours stay as they are.
beats.fizzled: The fights stop and so does the talk.

local.title: Opening on the day of rest
local.question: Should shops be allowed to open on the day of rest?

sides.name: Let them open
sides.stand: let shops open if they want

beats.whispers: A shop in {hood} opened its doors on the day of rest.
beats.open: The {office} is asked to rule on it.
beats.heated: Sermons across the city take aim at the shop.
beats.fizzled: Everyone goes back to how it was.

local.title: The show at {place}
local.question: Should the scandalous show at {place} be stopped?

beats.whispers: Everyone is talking about the show at {place}.
beats.open: A preacher names it from the pulpit.
beats.heated: Crowds of both sides fill the street outside.
beats.lost: The show runs on, sold out.
beats.fizzled: The show ends its run and the fuss with it.

local.title: Dogs in the park
local.question: Should dogs be banned from the park in {hood}?

sides.name: Let them run
sides.stand: let dogs run in the park

beats.whispers: A child was knocked over by a dog in {hood}.
beats.open: A ban is proposed.
beats.heated: Dog owners march through the park.
beats.fizzled: People keep their dogs on leads and the matter is dropped.

local.title: A curfew for the young
local.question: Should the young be kept off the streets after dark?

sides.name: Curfew
sides.stand: keep the young indoors after dark

beats.whispers: There has been trouble at night in {hood}.
beats.open: The {office2} asks for a curfew.
beats.heated: The young gather in the streets in defiance.
beats.fizzled: The trouble stops and the curfew is forgotten.

local.title: Calling off the fair
local.question: Should this year's fair be called off?

sides.name: Call it off
sides.stand: save the money and the trouble

beats.whispers: The fair costs more every year, people say.
beats.open: The {office} says it may be called off.
beats.heated: Stallholders and players march together.
beats.fizzled: A smaller fair is held.

local.title: The statue in {hood}
local.question: Should the old statue in {hood} come down?

beats.whispers: Someone painted over the statue's plaque in {hood}.
beats.open: A petition asks for it to come down.
beats.heated: A guard is put on the statue at night.
beats.fizzled: The paint is cleaned off and so is the matter.

local.title: What may be worn in public
local.question: Should the new fashions be banned in public?

sides.name: Ban them
sides.stand: keep decent dress on the streets

sides.name: Let people dress
sides.stand: let people wear what they like

beats.whispers: A new fashion has the old folks scandalized.
beats.open: A ban is put before the {office}.
beats.heated: The young wear it all the more.
beats.lost: The ban is laughed out of the chamber.
beats.fizzled: The fashion passes before the ban does.

local.title: The noise in {hood}
local.question: Should the music in {hood} stop at ten?

beats.whispers: Neighbors in {hood} are fed up with the late nights.
beats.open: A ten o'clock rule is proposed.
beats.heated: The clubs in {hood} play louder in protest.
beats.won: Quiet at ten becomes the rule.
beats.fizzled: A deal is struck: quiet at midnight.

local.title: The street preacher
local.question: Should the new preacher be let to preach in the square?

beats.whispers: A new preacher draws a crowd in {hood}.
beats.open: The {office2} tells the preacher to move on.
beats.heated: Followers fill the square.
beats.fizzled: The preacher leaves town on their own.

local.title: The lord's marriage fee
local.question: Should couples still pay the old fee to marry?

beats.whispers: A couple in {hood} could not pay the fee to marry.
beats.open: The priest marries them anyway.
beats.heated: The steward demands the fee.
beats.fizzled: The fee is quietly forgotten.

local.title: The game hall
local.question: Should the new game hall be allowed to stay open all night?

beats.whispers: The new game hall in {hood} never closes.
beats.open: Parents complain to the {office2}.
beats.heated: A fight at the hall turns it into a cause.
beats.fizzled: The hall goes out of fashion.

local.title: The {trade} strike
local.question: Should the {trade} get the raise they are striking for?

beats.whispers: The {trade} are talking about walking out.
beats.open: The {trade} walk out.
beats.heated: Strikebreakers are brought in and there are scuffles.
beats.lost: The strike breaks and they go back for nothing.
beats.fizzled: They go back with half of what they asked.

local.title: Who may join the {trade}
local.question: Should the {trade} let in newcomers without the old fees?

sides.name: Keep the fees
sides.stand: keep the old fees and the old ways
